correctness.rationale: Both supplied complete-state C++ implementations enumerate exactly \(4^{12}=16{,}777{,}216\) labelled \(q=4\) GHM states on the stated Chvátal adjacency. The indegree-peeling functional-graph proof and independent path-memoization algorithm give identical 21 (entry,period) classes and periods only 1 and 4, sharp entry 12 attained by 48 states. A third exhaustive local-coloring checker counts exactly 118408 successor-supported four-colorings; a rigorous connected-graph lemma equates these with nonzero period-four states. An independent exhaustive automorphism backtracking script proves 8 graph automorphisms and six size-8 orbits on the 48 maximal states. Finite enumeration proves only this fixed finite-graph claim; no asymptotic extrapolation is involved.

originality.rationale: Comparison with published mathematical records and accessible prior results found the same-graph prior census only for three colors, with a distinct six-period spectrum, and four-state results on nonisomorphic graph families. Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff and Doba treat finite-graph three-valued excitation; Durrett–Griffeath provide general multistate lattice context. The three-state results do not imply \(q=4\) periods, entrance cutoff, or extremal symmetry. Full \(q=4\) Chvátal priority remains subject to possible unindexed literature.

value.rationale: Chvátal is the smallest triangle-free 4-regular 4-chromatic graph, making four-state excitation a natural test case near a graph/color threshold. Increasing refractory length from three to four states deletes all prior \(q=3\) period-11 and other non-4 oscillations, yet raises the sharp first-entry time from 10 to 12; this nonmonotone spectral-versus-transient response is supported by the exact recurrent-state and basin census. Six distinct maximal symmetry classes and a structural local coloring criterion give reusable finite combinatorial data and test cases rather than arbitrary isolated numbers.
